headline: Massachusetts MCAS results show grade 8 math gains but wider ELA challenges
dek: The state says 42 percent of eighth-graders met or exceeded math expectations, while grades 3-8 ELA performance fell two points from 2025.
body: Massachusetts released its 2026 MCAS and school-accountability results Tuesday, reporting a notable improvement in eighth-grade math alongside continued gaps in English language arts and science.

The Department of Elementary and Secondary Education said 42 percent of eighth-graders met or exceeded expectations in math, up four percentage points from 2025. Across grades 3-8, 41 percent of students met or exceeded math expectations, roughly unchanged from last year.

English language arts results were weaker. Forty percent of students in grades 3-8 met or exceeded expectations, down two percentage points from 2025, while the grade 10 ELA rate fell six points to 45 percent. In science, eighth-grade performance rose two points to 39 percent, but fifth-grade and high-school results declined.

The release comes as Massachusetts moves beyond the former requirement that students earn a qualifying MCAS score to graduate. State officials are developing a broader graduation framework that includes rigorous coursework, end-of-course assessments, postsecondary planning and career or work-based learning.

DESE also said 80 percent of schools received accountability designations indicating they did not require state assistance or intervention, and 56 schools were selected for recognition based on strong improvement or overall achievement. Families can review statewide, district and school results through the department's MCAS reporting portal.
